title: Why map(parseInt) returns NaN
question: Number() or parseInt(str, 10)?
fact_source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/map#using_parseint_with_map (['1','2','3'].map(parseInt) gives [1, NaN, NaN]; map passes element, index, array and parseInt takes the index as radix; fix: map((str) => parseInt(str, 10)) or map(Number))

scenes.headline: map(parseInt) broke your array
scenes.voice: You map parse int over the strings one, two, three, and get one, then not a number, twice?
scenes.caption: You map parseInt over "1", "2", "3" and get 1, then NaN, twice?

scenes.headline: map passes the index as radix
scenes.voice: Map also passes the index, and parse int reads it as the radix. So two in base one is not a number.
scenes.caption: map also passes the index, and parseInt reads it as the radix. So "2" in base 1 is NaN.

scenes.headline: Pass one argument only
scenes.voice: Use map with Number, or an arrow function that calls parse int with radix ten.
scenes.caption: Use map(Number), or an arrow function that calls parseInt with radix 10.

scenes.headline: 3 of 3 values correct
scenes.voice: Now you get one, two, three. Three of three values right, not one.
scenes.caption: Now you get 1, 2, 3. Three of three values right, not one.

scenes.voice: Which do you use: Number, or parse int with radix ten? Comment your answer.
scenes.caption: Which do you use: Number(), or parseInt with radix 10? Comment your answer.
